new_entities.name: Polycythemia vera
new_entities.description: A myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by increased red cell mass and heightened thrombotic risk.

edges.effect_quant: A 2026 Swedish population study of 2,604 polycythemia vera patients found arterial event rates above 2 per 100 patient-years even on treatment, consistent with substantial residual cerebrovascular risk.
edges.mechanism: Polycythemia vera increases hematocrit, blood viscosity, leukocyte activation, and platelet-driven thrombosis, all of which can promote arterial occlusion including ischemic stroke. Uncontrolled counts and coexisting cardiovascular risk factors can amplify that baseline thrombotic tendency.
edges.summary: Polycythemia vera carries a clear excess thrombotic burden, and stroke belongs to that arterial-risk spectrum. Modern real-world cohorts and longstanding hematology reviews consistently show that cerebrovascular events remain a key complication, which is why hematocrit control and antithrombotic risk reduction are central in PV management.
edges.caveats: Many studies report arterial thrombosis as a composite rather than isolating stroke alone, so this edge is partly inferred from the well-established arterial-event burden in PV. Absolute stroke risk varies with age, prior thrombosis, leukocytosis, cardiovascular comorbidity, and adequacy of cytoreductive control.
